title: "Lecture 11 Team Projects"
subtitle: "Interest-Rate Options"
---

## Project 1: Cap, Floor, or Swap for a Borrower?

**Scenario.** Protect a floating-rate borrower against rising rates using a cap, swap, or no hedge.

**Objectives.** Compare payoff asymmetry, premium, opportunity cost, accounting, and liquidity; evaluate four rate scenarios; recommend within a risk budget.

**Sources.** Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) contract information from [CME Group](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/stirs/three-month-sofr.html), observed SOFR from the [Federal Reserve Bank of New York](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/sofr) or [Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SOFR), and a public floating-rate debt disclosure. If executable cap and swap quotes are unavailable, use the documented [Lecture 11 fallback rate-option and borrower snapshot](fallback_data/lecture-11-rate-options.csv).

**Deliverables.** Exposure profile, payoff table, scenario costs, volatility discussion, recommendation and trigger, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Setup 20; payoffs 30; option-versus-swap reasoning 20; recommendation 20; presentation 10.

## Project 2: Option on Treasury Futures Event Hedge

**Scenario.** Limit downside around a policy or inflation release without surrendering all upside.

**Objectives.** Choose a futures option or spread; map payoff to duration exposure; compare with a linear futures hedge.

**Sources.** Treasury futures and options data from [CME Group](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/us-treasury.html), plus event calendars from the [Federal Reserve](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm), [U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/), or [Bank of Canada](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/core-functions/monetary-policy/key-interest-rate/). If a dated option chain is unavailable, use the documented [Lecture 11 fallback rate-option and borrower snapshot](fallback_data/lecture-11-rate-options.csv).

**Deliverables.** Event definition, contract and strike, payoff diagram, premium-inclusive scenarios, hedge comparison, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Framing 15; selection 25; payoff calculations 25; hedge judgment 25; presentation 10.

## Project 3: Collar a Floating-Rate Liability

**Scenario.** Design a cap-and-floor collar for a borrower that wants a bounded interest rate at limited net premium.

**Objectives.** Choose cap and floor strikes; calculate all-in borrowing costs across scenarios; explain premium, basis, counterparty, and opportunity-cost tradeoffs.

**Sources.** Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) futures and options from [CME Group](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/stirs/three-month-sofr.html) and observed SOFR from the [Federal Reserve Bank of New York](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/sofr). If market premiums or loan terms are unavailable, use the documented cap, floor, and loan inputs in the [Lecture 11 fallback rate-option and borrower snapshot](fallback_data/lecture-11-rate-options.csv).

**Deliverables.** Instrument terms, payoff chart, six-scenario cost table, comparison with cap-only and swap alternatives, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Structure design 25; payoff accuracy 25; comparison 20; risk and recommendation 20; presentation and documentation 10.

## Project 4: Volatility and Option Value Briefing

**Scenario.** Explain why two otherwise similar rate options have different premiums and how a volatility change affects a hedge budget.

**Objectives.** Compare intrinsic and time value; explain expiry, moneyness, volatility, and rates; test low/base/high volatility quotes; recommend a structure.

**Sources.** Contract specifications and delayed quotes from [CME Group](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates.html), plus benchmark rates from [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/categories/22) or the [U.S. Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView). If comparable volatility and premium quotes are unavailable, use the documented low, base, and high volatility cases in the [Lecture 11 fallback rate-option and borrower snapshot](fallback_data/lecture-11-rate-options.csv).

**Deliverables.** Option comparison, premium decomposition, three-volatility sensitivity, budget tradeoff, recommendation, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Instrument comparison 20; value-driver analysis 25; sensitivity 25; recommendation 20; presentation and sources 10.
